Correlation Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch64.R
centrality_correlation_centrality.Rd

Correlation centrality (Fan et al. 2013) sums the efficiency of the other nodes, each weighted by the number of shortest paths to it and discounted by a power of the distance: $$CoC(i) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j \ne i} EC(j) \frac{\sigma_{ij}}{d_{ij}^{\alpha}}, \qquad EC(j) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k \ne j} \frac{1}{d_{jk}},$$ with \(\sigma_{ij}\) the number of shortest paths between \(i\) and \(j\) and \(d_{ij}\) their distance.

Usage

centrality_correlation_centrality(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses coc_alpha (the exponent of the distance, default 3).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. coc_alpha is 3 by default, the value the source selects. With that value the direct neighbors carry most of the score. A node that cannot be reached contributes 0, and isolated nodes score 0. The implementation reproduces the 21 values the source prints for the ARPA network, on an edge list recovered from the other columns of the same table. A coc_alpha that is not a single finite nonnegative number raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Fan, W., Liu, Z. and Hu, P. (2013). Identifying node importance based on information entropy in complex networks. Physica Scripta, 88(6), 065201. doi:10.1088/0031-8949/88/06/065201 .

See also

centrality_harmonic, centrality_niccm, centrality.

Examples

centrality_correlation_centrality(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   0.470625   0.538125   0.570000   0.562500   0.494375   0.499375   0.423750 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   0.503750   0.533125   0.486875
